lead_time_analysis.stability: Moderate — 1 outlier detected (2.73 days); otherwise consistent short lead times

narrative: Material PL1__MC328F79 exhibits stable, normally distributed daily demand averaging 448 units with a CV of 0.34 and no statistically significant trend. Lead times are short (mean 1.03 days) but moderately variable (CV 0.49), with one outlier at 2.73 days. The (r,Q) policy was selected because the high ordering cost relative to holding cost favours large, infrequent replenishments; the EOQ of 6,690 units is capped to 5,868 by the 6,320-unit storage constraint. Establishing a safety stock of 451 units raises the reorder point to 914 and delivers 30.5% annual cost savings versus the current SAP policy.

research_insights.selected_model: (r, Q) continuous-review policy with EOQ-derived order quantity
research_insights.selection_rationale: Stable, normally distributed demand with 100% non-zero fraction and no trend makes the classical (r,Q) model optimal. The high ordering cost (50 USD) relative to low unit holding cost drives a large batch size, well-suited to the EOQ framework. Continuous review is preferred over periodic review given the short mean lead time of 1.03 days.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage cap reduces EOQ by ~12.3% (6690 → 5868 units), slightly increasing order frequency. The post-replenishment inventory (451+5868=6319) leaves only ~0.76 units of headroom — any upward revision of safety stock must be accompanied by a storage capacity review.
research_insights.escalation_flag: None — MOQ (2451) + safety_stock (451) = 2902 < max_storage_units (6319.762). Policy is feasible.
